title: Account settings
summary: A person had two settings pages and two privacy pages. /space/settings and /account/settings both edited the same photo, name and language on the user record, but each held only some controls: time zone, theme and notifications were only in the Space, and password, two-step verification, passkeys and devices only in /account. /account/privacy was a signpost to /space/privacy. The fix is one home for everything about the person, /account, in short pages (Profile, Notifications, Security, Privacy, Workspaces, Billing for practices), with a strict hierarchy: one headline and one line per page, one title and one line per card, a hint only where it prevents a mistake or says who sees a value, and background explanation in an (i) popover.
strengths: The cards, Lora headings and one teal action per block are calm and on brand; the merge keeps them.
Every control already went through apps/api (/me, /users, /privacy) with Zod and audit, so moving the pages needs no API change.
Privacy was complete: consents, a data copy with status, and deletion with a 14-day waiting period that can be cancelled.
Passkeys, two-step verification and Google linking were already wired to Better Auth.

findings.title: Two settings pages and two privacy pages for the same person
findings.detail: /space/settings and /account/settings both edit the photo, name and language stored on the user, with different wording for the same card. Time zone, theme and notifications exist only in the Space; password, two-step verification, passkeys, Google and devices only in /account. /account/privacy only describes three controls and links to /space/privacy. A member cannot tell which page is the real one, and asks whether she must set things up twice.
findings.recommendation: One home for everything about the person: /account. Pages: Profile (photo, name, email, language, time zone, appearance), Notifications, Security, Privacy, Workspaces, and Billing only for practices and clinics. /space/settings and /space/privacy redirect there, and the Space sidebar keeps Settings and Privacy under an 'Account' group that opens /account.

findings.title: Notification switches promise choices Eleva does not honour
findings.detail: The grid lets a member untick Payments and System, but those messages are always sent (REQUIRED_NOTIFICATION_CATEGORIES). It offers SMS and quiet hours, but texts need a verified phone number that nothing collects, and quiet hours only apply to texts. The Marketing row changes nothing: news emails follow the marketing consent on the Privacy page. A member can turn off session emails, which carry her join link.
findings.recommendation: Show only real choices. Sessions and reminders: email and in-app switches that save at once (the backend honours them). Payments and Account and security: switches that are on and locked, marked 'Always on'. Point news from Eleva to the Privacy page. Bring back text messages and quiet hours together with adding and verifying a mobile number.

findings.title: Sign-up does not record Terms and Privacy acceptance
findings.detail: Consents are written by the booking funnel and guest activation only. A person who signs up and has not booked has no Terms or Privacy row, so the old page showed 'Grant' next to Terms of use and Privacy notice for a signed-up member. The new page shows 'Updated {date}' with a Read link in that case, but the record itself is missing.
findings.recommendation: Record terms and privacy (current CONSENT_DOCUMENT_VERSION) when the account is created, from the sign-up screen's agreement, through @eleva/compliance with audit. Then 'What you agreed to' shows 'Agreed on {date}' for everyone. Needs legal review of the sign-up wording.

findings.title: Security mixed into profile, with raw device strings and a hidden 2FA step
findings.detail: Password, two-factor, passkeys, Google and sessions are one card under the profile. The password form shows to people who sign in with Google or an email link. 'Enable authenticator' silently uses the current-password field and prints a raw otpauth URI. Sessions list 29 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0…' strings with 'Revoke', no 'this device' and no way to sign out of all others.
findings.recommendation: A Security page: Password (or one line saying none is needed), Two-step verification as a short dialog (password, setup key with copy and an app link, backup codes, code), Passkeys with a list and an empty state, Google, and 'Where you're signed in' with 'Chrome on macOS', 'This device', last active, 'Sign out' and 'Sign out of all other devices'.

findings.title: No hierarchy between headline, title, hint and help
findings.detail: Every page repeats an 'ACCOUNT' eyebrow the sidebar already shows. Footers repeat the title or say things that are not true or not useful ('Email and identity changes may require verification', 'These preferences are used when we start sending notifications', 'Optional. Both start and end are required when enabled.'). The photo relies on 'Click the photo'. Long legal text sits on the page while short help has nowhere to go. The language select overlaps its title on phones.
findings.recommendation: Headline and one line per page, no eyebrow. Card: title and one line on why it matters. Field: label, and a hint only when it prevents a mistake or says who sees the value. Footer: state or consequence, then the action. Background in an (i) popover with an accessible name. What a member must know before an irreversible step goes in the confirm dialog.

findings.title: Billing offers expert and clinic plans to members
findings.detail: A member with no practice sees Expert Community, Top Expert (pre-selected), Clinic Starter and Clinic Growth, and 'Start an embedded Stripe Checkout session'. Plan names and descriptions are hard-coded in English.
findings.recommendation: Show Billing only to people with an expert practice or a clinic; a member who opens the address sees that receipts live in her Space with a link to Payments. Plan copy, translations and moving plans into practice settings follow in the expert consistency pass.

findings.title: Consent switches carry the whole notice inline
findings.detail: Health data, news and AI each showed long paragraphs and a bullet list under the switch, so the Privacy page read as a legal wall.
findings.recommendation: Layered notice: each row shows the purpose, what it covers and what turning it on means in one line (health data names 'health information' and who uses it); a 'Details' dialog holds the bullets and the link to the full notice. News needs no Details.

references.pattern: Security as short sections: sessions, passkeys, apps
references.why: 'Security & access' stacks Sessions ('Devices logged into your account'), Passkeys and API keys, each a heading with one line under it. The current session is first, marked 'Current session' with a location; other sessions sit under '1 other session' with 'Revoke all'. Passkeys shows 'No passkeys registered' and a 'New passkey' button. Product tool, kept for its structure.
references.apply: Eleva Security: one card per sign-in method, the current device first and marked 'This device', a 'Sign out of all other devices' action, and an empty passkey state in words.
references.query: security settings with active sessions and devices list

references.pattern: Account settings split into named sections, with a hint under each setting
references.why: 'Account settings' has sections (Profile, Appearance, Account Security, Delete Account) listed on the right. Each setting has a label with a one-line hint under it ('Choose the theme that works best for you') and the control beside it. Developer tool, kept for its structure.
references.apply: Split Eleva's single long settings page into named pages in the sidebar, and give each setting a label plus at most one line of hint.
references.query: account settings page with a sidebar of sections

references.pattern: Section title, one line of purpose, then fields with a hint under each label
references.why: Each card has a bold title and one grey line on what it is for ('Manage your basic profile details'). Fields have a label and a short hint ('This is your full name as it will appear on your profile'). The photo card states the format under the upload button ('PNG, JPEG under 2MB'). 'Back to Dashboard' sits at the bottom of the sidebar. Product tool, kept for its structure.
references.apply: Eleva cards: title, one line on why it matters to the member, then fields; the photo has an explicit 'Upload a photo' button with the format hint beside it, not a hidden 'click the photo'.
references.query: account settings page with a sidebar of sections

references.pattern: Field hints that say who sees the value
references.why: Profile fields carry one-line hints that answer who sees them: 'Your full name. Visible to your team members.' and 'Your public name. Visible to customers.' Support tool, kept for its writing pattern.
references.apply: Eleva's details card says who sees the photo and name: 'Experts see your photo and name when you book with them.'
references.query: account settings page with a sidebar of sections

references.pattern: Signed-in devices in plain words, with a sign-out per device
references.why: 'Check where you're signed in' explains the list in one sentence and recommends signing out of devices you no longer use or recognise. Each row reads 'Mac · Chrome' with a date and a 'Sign out' link. Consumer travel app.
references.apply: Name the devices card in member words ('Where you're signed in'), show 'Chrome on macOS', and say what to do about a device you don't recognise.
references.query: security settings with active sessions and devices list

references.pattern: This device badge and the next step for a suspicious sign-in
references.why: 'Active devices' lists 'Chrome, Mac OS' with a 'THIS DEVICE' badge on the current one and 'Log out' on the others. Under the list: 'If you notice any suspicious logins, we recommend logging the suspicious device out, enabling two-factor authentication, and changing the password'. CRM, kept for its structure.
references.apply: A 'This device' badge instead of a sign-out on the current session, and the one-line advice in the card description.
references.query: security settings with active sessions and devices list

references.pattern: Background explanation in a small popover, not on the page
references.why: On 'Tip settings', the value 'Recipient keeps tips' has a dotted underline; hovering shows 'Each team member keeps 100% of the tips they collect.' The page itself stays one line per row. Business tool, kept for the pattern.
references.apply: Eleva's info popover holds background a member may want but does not need to act (what a passkey is, how AI help works, where 'In Eleva' messages appear). What she must know before acting stays on the page or in the confirm dialog.
references.query: settings form with info icon tooltip explaining a field

references.pattern: A help icon next to a setting's label
references.why: 'Secure requests' has a (?) icon next to the label; the switch row carries one sentence on what it changes and a 'Learn about secure requests' link. Accounting tool, kept for the pattern.
references.apply: Put the (i) next to the section title or label it explains, give it an accessible name ('About passkeys'), and keep one sentence of hint on the page.
references.query: settings form with info icon tooltip explaining a field

references.pattern: Two-step setup as one goal per step, with 'Step 2 of 3' and what comes next
references.why: 'Enable an authenticator app' runs in three steps inside one dialog: install an app, scan the QR code, enter the 6-digit code. Each step has one heading and one action; the footer reads 'Step: 2 of 3 · Next: Link an authenticator app' beside 'Next', and a back arrow returns to the previous step. The QR code is large, with 'Can't scan the QR Code?' under it. Payroll product, kept for its structure.
references.apply: Eleva's two-step dialog: confirm the password, scan, enter the code, then save backup codes, each its own step with 'Step x of 4', Back and one primary button.
references.query: setting up two-factor authentication with an authenticator app

references.pattern: The setup key hides behind 'Can't scan QR code?'; backup codes come after setup
references.why: The scan step shows only the QR code, a 'Can't scan QR code?' link and the 6-digit field. Once the app is on, the page offers 'Generate' for backup codes as a separate action. Developer tool, kept for its structure.
references.apply: Show the key only when someone asks for it, and show backup codes after the code is accepted, as the last step.
references.query: setting up two-factor authentication with an authenticator app

references.pattern: Each privacy switch has a title and one line, with 'Learn more' for the rest
references.why: The page stays short: one sentence says what the switch does, and the detail is one click away.
references.apply: Consent rows show the purpose and what turning it on means in one line; a 'Details' dialog holds the bullets and the notice link.
references.query: privacy settings with consent toggles and a learn more link that opens details

references.pattern: Short consequence line under each switch, 'Learn more' inline
references.why: Every switch says what changes for you in a few words; nothing explains the mechanics on the page.
references.apply: Keep the visible line to the consequence ('You need this on to book', 'Off unless you turn it on'); no Details for simple choices like news.
references.query: privacy settings with consent toggles and a learn more link that opens details

judging_criteria: Is there exactly one place to change each personal setting, and do old Space addresses land there? (12-account-settings/02)

Does every page have one headline and one line, every card one title and one line, and does each hint either prevent a mistake or say who sees a value? (12-account-settings/03, 12-account-settings/04)

Is background help in an (i) popover with an accessible name, while what a member must know before deleting her account stays in the dialog she confirms? (12-account-settings/07, 12-account-settings/08)
Does every notification switch change what Eleva sends, with 'Always on' where it cannot? (12-account-settings/01)
Can she tell at a glance what she agreed to (dated, readable) apart from the choices she can switch on and off? (10-member-space/08)
Does the devices list name devices in plain words, mark this device, and let her sign out of the others in one step? (12-account-settings/05, 12-account-settings/06)
On a 390 px screen, does every page fit without sideways scrolling, with actions on the same line as the row they belong to? (12-account-settings/01)

Does each consent switch say, in one visible line, what it is for and what turning it on means, with the rest one tap away in Details and the full notice linked? (12-account-settings/11, 12-account-settings/12)
